messages.subject: processData(survreg.fit()) model did not converge
parts:
First, I'd like to say I think MSstats is a fantastic tool and I'm so grateful it exists. I'm using it to process data for the final chapter of my thesis!

Second, I'd really like some guidance on an error I encountered at the early stage, running processData().

I'm using the MSstats.csv output of FragPipe. There are 4 condition, 3 biological replicates, but one biological replicate of one condition has 2 technical replicates.

This is the workflow:
library(MSstats)

# Read MSstats.csv file.
raw <- read_csv("MSstats.csv"), na = c("", "NA", "0"))
raw$ProteinName <- factor(raw$ProteinName)
raw$PeptideSequence <- factor(raw$PeptideSequence)

# Processing the data using MSstats
processedData <- dataProcess(raw, logTrans = 10)
[please see attached log, after which the following warnings are displayed:]
Warning messages: 1: In survreg.fit(X, Y, weights, offset, init = init, controlvals = control, : Ran out of iterations and did not converge 2: In survreg.fit(X, Y, weights, offset, init = init, controlvals = control, : Ran out of iterations and did not converge 3: In survreg.fit(X, Y, weights, offset, init = init, controlvals = control, : Ran out of iterations and did not converge 4: In survreg.fit(X, Y, weights, offset, init = init, controlvals = control, : Ran out of iterations and did not converge

I'm not sure what to do here. Is there a way to increase the number of iterations, somehow? Or is this indicative of a particular issue with the data? I would really appreciate any help.

Here is a link to the file: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EmtTvc6-UVCWfkHzq0sgjtKDf2oq3Pzi/view?usp=sharing 

Thank you!

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: processData(survreg.fit()) model did not converge
parts:
Hello,

These warnings actually come from the missing value imputation (MBimpute=TRUE in the parameters). We fit the missing values with the survreg.fit function, and if the function fails to converge then you will see this warning. This generally happens when we do not have enough information to impute. In cases where the model does not converge, you should see those values left NA. I've run your data and the imputed values look generally reasonable as far as I can tell. As such I think you are ok to ignore these warnings.

In general with missing value imputation I would always recommend taking a closer look at the imputed values using profile plots to ensure that they make sense. 

Best,
Devon

parts:
Hi Devon,

Thank you so much for checking the data and for responding to me! I'm so relieved that I can probably go ahead with this without issues.

Can you please clarify what I should look for in profile plots? Is it the difference in feature-level data and run summary?

Also, this might be a stretch to ask but I just wanted your advice on whether you think it's a good idea to remove one of my biological replicates (of 3). Its run didn't go well so we ran it again (hence the two technical replicates for only one sample), but that also didn't go very well, so this biological replicate looks quite different than the other 2 biological replicates for the same condition in some of the plots (both profile and QC; see attached examples). Plus, the two technical replicates of this biological replicate had > 75% missing values. I understand if you feel you can't offer advice here, but if you have some thoughts, I'd really appreciate them.

Thank you again!
Majd
